Let \( ABC \) be an isosceles triangle with \( AB = AC \). Points \( P \) and \( Q \) are located inside triangle \( ABC \) such that \( BP = PQ = QC \). Suppose that \( \angle BAP = 20^\circ \), \( \angle PAQ = 46^\circ \), and \( \angle QAC = 26^\circ \). Compute the measure of \( \angle APC \) in degrees.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(AB=AC=1\).  Put

\[
AP=x,\qquad AQ=y.
\]

The given angles at \(A\) give

\[
\angle BAP=20^\circ,\quad \angle PAQ=46^\circ,\quad \angle QAC=26^\circ,
\]

so \(\angle BAC=92^\circ\).

Using the law of cosines in \(\triangle ABP,\triangle APQ,\triangle AQC\), the condition \(BP=PQ=QC\) gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
BP^2&=1+x^2-2x\cos20^\circ,\\
PQ^2&=x^2+y^2-2xy\cos46^\circ,\\
QC^2&=1+y^2-2y\cos26^\circ.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus

\[
\begin{cases}
1-2x\cos20^\circ=y^2-2xy\cos46^\circ,\\[2mm]
1-2y\cos26^\circ=x^2-2xy\cos46^\circ.
\end{cases}\tag{1}
\]

The system has a unique admissible interior solution.  One convenient way to identify it is to check the following values.

Let

\[
S=\sin74^\circ.
\]

Try

\[
x=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{S},\qquad y=\frac{\sin40^\circ}{S}.
\]

Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
BP^2&=\frac{S^2+\sin^2 34^\circ-2S\sin34^\circ\cos20^\circ}{S^2},\\
PQ^2&=\frac{\sin^2 34^\circ+\sin^2 40^\circ-2\sin34^\circ\sin40^\circ\cos46^\circ}{S^2},\\
QC^2&=\frac{S^2+\sin^2 40^\circ-2S\sin40^\circ\cos26^\circ}{S^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using product-to-sum identities,

\[
S^2-\sin^2 40^\circ=\sin66^\circ\sin34^\circ,
\]

and

\[
2(\sin40^\circ\cos46^\circ-S\cos20^\circ)
=-(\sin6^\circ+\sin54^\circ)=-\cos24^\circ.
\]

Since \(\sin66^\circ=\cos24^\circ\), the first two numerators are equal.

Similarly,

\[
S^2-\sin^2 34^\circ=\sin72^\circ\sin40^\circ,
\]

and

\[
2(S\cos26^\circ-\sin34^\circ\cos46^\circ)
=\sin48^\circ+\sin12^\circ=\cos18^\circ=\sin72^\circ.
\]

Hence the second and third numerators are also equal.  Therefore

\[
BP=PQ=QC.
\]

So the unique interior solution is indeed

\[
AP=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ},\qquad AQ=\frac{\sin40^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

Now in \(\triangle APC\),

\[
\angle PAC=\angle PAQ+\angle QAC=46^\circ+26^\circ=72^\circ,
\]

and

\[
\frac{AP}{AC}=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

By the sine rule, the angles opposite \(AC\) and \(AP\) must be \(74^\circ\) and \(34^\circ\), respectively.  Hence

\[
\angle APC=74^\circ.
\]

\[
\boxed{74}
\]
